Showcase Russian Culture
desc: The OFN is up to this point almost or entirely made of countries traditionally considered part of the West. Due to decades of chaos within the former Soviet Union, America and her allies have paid little attention to Russia up until very recently. Therefore, a biased cosmopolitanism exists amongst the peoples of the Free World, whose stereotypes hinder our efforts to join them. We must break through this underlying, subconscious Orientalism if we are to join the Americans as peers.

name: Visit OFN Military Bases
desc: OFN has been most reclusive to foreign powers, and they have a very good reason for doing so. However, President Koryagin's reputation as a peacemaker precedes him and his followers. Though we love peace, the  RSLP still understands the necessity to defend freedom from the horde of fascism. Visiting OFN military installations will signal that the Russians are ready to learn and engage in further cooperation with OFN militarily.

name: Tour the Free World
desc: Throughout history, very few Russian rulers chose to venture beyond the borders of our motherland. Indeed, there are too many works at hand, but let us not forget that before Shukshin, another great leader of the Russian people embraced his western allies and together with them vanquished their shared foes. Koryagin will follow the footsteps of Peter the Great towards the bastions of freedom in the West!

name: Expand Trade Links
desc: Prior to the Second West Russian War, the main hub of Russo-American trade was Magadan. Though a grand port as a result of multiple expansions, the vast distance between it and major population centers rendered it ineffective. However, now that our rule has been cemented in Western Russia, more seaward trading routes are becoming available, such as Murmansk and St. Petersburg. With a little nudge on our tariffs and policies, a never-ending stream of Russian freighters and sailors will speak louder than any of our diplomats.

name: Apply for OFN Membership
desc:
Russia was thought to be the manifestation of the East: a wild, rabid steppe that mothers the eternal enemy of Western civilization. It was thought that Russian Federation would become an enemy as potent as the German Reich once was to the United States and its allies. President Koryagin has smashed those stereotypes harbored by cynical international political analysts. Instead of rivalry, Russians have only grown closer to the Western world as a friend of democracy.

With our joining of the OFN, fascism will be sniffed out.

name: The  VRPP is campaigning against the OFN!
Meet with Veterans
desc: Many veterans of the Smuta and the subsequent Second West Russian War choose to oppose the efforts of  RSLP to join the OFN mainly due to their concerns over Russian sovereignty after our incorporation into the alliance. They, and the general public, must understand that Russia can and will stand on equal footing to the United States.

name: Reassure Moderates
desc: Some moderate members of the  All-Russian Patriotic Party are concerned about the potential damage to the Russian economy. They understand that Russia will certainly choose to integrate into the global, Western market, but fear the potential loss of jobs as a result of globalization. We will make it abundantly clear that while we respect our friends, not even the Americans may hurt our national growth!

name: Endorse Pro-OFN Propaganda
desc: We shall make use of political propaganda within and without the country to pressure our opposition. While the  VRPP may attack our party for "selling out the nation", we must stress how much the Americans have aided us throughout our struggle. Producing films and documentaries highlighting the brotherly bond between our countries will sway some of the less engaged nationalists.

name: Appease Corporate Executives
desc: Many businessmen won their place in Russia simply because they copied American models, and therefore fear what will happen once their American competitors start to pour resources into the Russian market. While undesirable, we must reach compromises with these leading companies, especially on protecting Russian businesses, so they won't become mouthpieces of the  VRPP!

name: Talk with Shukshin
desc: Though Vasily Shukshin is a friend of democracy and freedom, he considers Russian sovereignty just as crucial. A long advocate for the establishment of a Russia-led Eurasian coalition, his status as a liberator of the nation greatly affects the  RAPP's opinion on the OFN. Let us remind him of the benefits of international cooperation, and the prospect of  VRPP taking advantage of our potential failure if he does not work with us. Surely Shukshin will favour liberals any day over greedy oligarchs.

name: The  DSPR is campaigning against the OFN!
Promise Worker Concessions
desc: Appeasing workers and the nascent trade unions of indigenous Russian businesses is critical. While we support globalized trade that will, in the long term, bring prosperity to all, we cannot pretend that globalization will not hurt working people who supported us. We can promise some protections, but we must emphasize that we cannot rock the boat when we are so close to joining the biggest trade bloc in the world!

name: Reach Out to the Disenfranchised
desc: The United States, despite all its political discourse, has been a model democracy, one that Russia is still learning from. A significant chunk of the  DSPR's supporters either belong to national minorities or those who feel the government has not done enough to extend freedom and autonomy. To deprive the Democratic Socailists of support, we will use our governmental and party media to hint at the  RSLP's willingness to adopt Western federal models and other democratic institutions.

name: Discredit Radical Communists
desc: The KPRF, SRs, and some less-than-savory authoritarian factions of the  DSPR have been attacking the  RSLP regime for its preparation to "import capitalist misery and chaos from America into the Russian Federation". However, one will be quick to see Koryagin's plans include nothing of the exploitative sort, and has been working on international fraternity more than the Communists have ever done so. Let's make it clear to the people.

name: Acknowledge Past Mistakes
desc: In the past, the  Silovki persecuted the predecessor of the  DSPR. The Narodniks were heavily oppressed by the past regime, which led to many avoidable tragedies. Now that a new, more humane party is in charge, we should try to work to rehabilitate and apologize to the victims on the  Silovki's behalf. Though the  DSPR, SRs, and KPRF will appreciate this gesture, the  VRPP will dislike us for pardoning "terrorist syndicalists".

name: Talk with Kantorovich
desc: Leonid Kantorovich is the embodiment of the mainstream Russian Left, which still harbors concerns over our support of globalization via joining the OFN. Compared to Primakov, we should be able to extract more support from him, if we can provide some meaningful promises on protecting workers from over-the-top trade agreements. A lunch or two with President Koryagin should clear him of all concerns if we cooperate with the  DSPR and amend our goals to take the voice of Russian workers into account.

name: Crush Defeatist Sentiments
desc: Even as victory is at hand there are still those who would prefer humiliation beneath the German jackboot over doing their part to achieve final victory. The Black Hand will bring them into line.

name: Integrate Kazakhstan
desc: We will work with Russian leaders in the Kazakh area to slowly integrate the region into our nation. This process will be slow, but not as slow or painful as it would be without any local assistance whatsoever.

name: Intervention in the Iranian Civil War
Add Russia to the Cold War Interface
Encourage International Volunteers
desc: In the past, the Soviet Union organized international forces in collaboration with local communist parties, fostering a spirit of solidarity in our collective struggle. A lot has changed since the thirties and now it's the Soviet Union itself that needs help. As the rightful seat of the Soviet government, we'll reach out to the remaining socialist movements of the world to organize volunteer forces to be sent to us through the port of Magadan. While this will help us with our regrettable manpower situation, these men and women are not of the highest quality, even under NKVD supervision.

name: Begin the 9th Five Year Plan
desc: With the initial underperformance of the last Five Year Plan remedied thanks to the reclamation of more parts of the Soviet Union and the restoration of its resources to rightful Soviet rule, S.D.R.C. has revised their projections for the Eighth plan. With its successful completion according to our economists projections, the Soviet Union's economic strength will surpass what we had before the outbreak of the Siberian War!

name: Repair the Highway
desc: The M55 Highway connecting the temporary Soviet capital to the rest of Siberia has been badly damaged as a result of the recent uprising by the revisionist agitators under Sablin. As we've already dealt with their punishments for this insurrection, we'll use this as an opportunity to rehabilitate some of his former men by assigning them to a state construction firm. They should be thankful that we're giving them a path back to socialist labor - the other rebels will not be as lucky...

name: Finish the Highway
desc: One of the issues noted by our economists is the lack of functional trains and reliable roads as a result of the persistent efforts of the enemies of the people to disrupt Soviet rule in Siberia. While those leading out of the temporary Soviet capital are serviceable, the same can't be said about the recently reclaimed areas to the east. It's therefore of the utmost importance that we restore the roads to working condition so that we may continue with our economic development. Started in the past decades as part of the Siberian Plan, the M58 connecting Chita to Amur was left unfinished due to the Great Patriotic War and the subsequent disruptions in communications. Organizing a supplemental labor battalion out of the RFP prisoners from the liberation of Amur should ensure the swift completion of the project. Justice will be dispensed as their masters in Berlin caused this unfortunate delay in the first place.

name: Complete the Magadan Connection
desc: The M56 was an endeavor to connect Magadan to the more temperate parts of Siberia. Many laborers risked life and limb to achieve this monument to socialist progress, but just like they've destroyed so many things in the Soviet Union, the fascists that occupied the port of Magadan have let most of the oblast's infrastructure go to waste. Justice shall be swift, and the NKVD will make sure that a labour detail consisting of Matkovsky's captured men repair every last inch of the road that they wrecked. Once we have a decent road leading into Magadan, we can finally begin transporting goods to and from the port.

name: Reconstruction of the Irkutsk Hydropower Station
desc: During previous difficult times, we lacked the necessary industrial equipment to effectively maintain the Irkutsk Hydropower Station. Consequently, the station was severely overloaded, and power generation fell short of expectations. However, with the complete liberation of the Far East, we are finally able to restore this industrial gem. Not only will it provide a steady supply of electricity for economic development, but the restoration work itself will also increase government procurement and promote industrial development in the Union.

name: Restore the Agricultural Sector
desc: After the Russian Fascist Party completely abandoned Soviet central farmland planning, the Amur fields were transformed from Siberia's greatest breadbasket into a desolate, frozen wasteland. The Ministry of Agriculture and Food, having estimated the manpower required to restore grain production to pre-war Siberia levels, recommends that we use this difficult period of peace to return some conscripted peasants to their traditional occupations and balance the number of peasants with some of the recently liberated population in secondary sectors. While agriculture is no longer a vital component of a modern industrial economy, as it was at the birth of our Union, a complete transition to an industrial economy is unrealistic if the majority of the population is starving.

name: Expand the Port
desc: Foreign trade is essential to our future economic development. We need to further expand the port's capacity, while also expanding our icebreaker fleet and navigational capabilities. Once we complete this expansion, we will have a solid foundation for our next five-year plan.

name: Rapid Factory Modernization
desc: With our improved access to the outside world comes the obvious benefits of having easier access to industrial equipment. While our landlocked rivals in the west struggle to get their hands on modern machinery as they're surrounded by uncooperative rogue states, our access to the sea changes the situation entirely. With the recent expansion of Magadan's facilities, we're in a good position to import the kind of machinery we need to revitalize our industrial economy.

name: Revive the Mining Industry
desc: Beneath the surface of Siberia lies vast, untapped riches. Coal, gold, diamonds, iron ore, and a myriad of valuable minerals are right at our fingertips, but sadly cannot currently be excavated due to many of our mines falling into disrepair during the anarchy. By importing equipment and schematics from abroad, we can undo years of decay in short order.

name: Trade with the Developing World
desc: While our economy was never officially closed, it has understandably been struggling due to the anarchy putting development into a state of abject stasis. Despite the many disagreements that [RUS.GetLeader] and the Party factions have, this is one area where they see common ground as trade with friendly and neutral states in Asia and across the Pacific can work in harmony both with the old Bukharinite system and the coexistence between Marxism and capitalism envisioned by some of our newer economists. With products to offer the world and a profound need for goods to bolster our economy, we'll initiate efforts to restore trade ties with former partners in the developing world and seek out new trade ties as well.

name: Modernize the irkutsk HPS
desc: The turbines used in the irkutsk HPS linger back to the days of the Siberian Plan. While not a direct target in any of the recent wars, the aftershocks caused by the fall of Moscow and the Siberian War can still be felt to this day. By purchasing equipment on the foreign markets and hiring experts to help us modernize the plants to the standards of this decade, the provisory capital of the Soviet Union will be ranked among the most important electricity production stations in all of Asia. Needless to say, this will go a long way to achieve the goals of our Five Year Plan by ensuring plentiful of electricity day and night, all year around for both common citizens, state industries and investors alike.

name: The Economic Heart of Siberia
desc: Our renovation and revitalization of the current seat of Soviet power must not be a half-measure. As the most advanced city in the Soviet Union, irkutsk will take the first steps into being a modern economy. Avoiding reckless marches into the unknown, we'll limit the Union's evolution into a more contemporary economic model to take the shape of gradual steps, starting out by tweaking the legal framework for businesses in the city as well as investing in the creation of state service companies. Whereas we relied on raw industrial strength in the past, the economy of the new Union will be known for its efficiency as well.

name: Expanded Brigade Recruitment
desc: With war on the horizon, we might want to look into expanding our volunteer recruitment and lower the standards for the volunteers that we do accept as well as providing volunteers with easier travel to the Union. While the influx of spirited men and women of strong socialist convictions is undoubtedly going to strengthen us, it will put a further strain on our efforts to train our army.

name: The Second Industrialization Wave
desc: In order to achieve our industrial goals, a second wave of investments into the state's heavy industry sector is needed. It'll be a broad push for industrial growth across the Union, seeing the construction and local modernizations of several factory complexes in all our major cities.

name: irkutsk Special Economic Sector
desc: After taking the first step towards modernizing our temporary capital's economy, it's time to take the next one. Avoiding the mistake of taking a great leap forward, we'll limit the reform package to opening up parts of irkutsk's central areas to foreign investments and provide generous legal and tax incentives to attract foreign capital with the state driving the push towards a service-based economic model for the city.

name: Yakutia Special Economic Province
desc: Back during the early days of the NEP's implementation it wasn't unheard of for British and Japanese mining companies to invest in the Soviet Union. [RUS.GetLeader] believes that with the right tax incentives, Yakutia could become a hotbed for foreign mining companies seeking to establish themselves on Soviet soil. Naturally, we'll make sure that our most important strategic resources remain firmly under the control of the State.

name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Open Coastal City
desc: With our efforts to approach the OFN bearing fruit, the Chairman believes that we need to strike while the iron is hot. As our closest territory to America, we'll declare Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky as an additional OCC and use state incentives to create an investment climate that's attractive to American technology companies. Naturally, we will arrange matters so that we can benefit from their expertise as well...

name: The Open Coastal City of Vladivostok
desc: As we advance towards realizing the [RUS.GetLeader] scheme, it's time that we put theory into practice. Vladivostok will be the major port where we will initiate a full-scale experiment in our new economic theory of two systems co-existing in the Soviet Union, reaping the rewards of a more modern economy.

name: The Industrial Harbor of Vladivostok
desc: With those seeking to betray the revolution and compromise with capitalism having lost the economic debate, it's time for us to move towards reaching the goals of our Five Year Plan. Through a heavy industrialization scheme that builds upon the successes of the Siberian Plan while also learning from its mistakes, we'll bring more prosperity to our Union.

name: The Tenth Five-Year Plan
desc: The Tenth Five-Year Plan under the leadership of Chairman [RUS.GetLeader] has achieved tremendous success, proving the correctness of [RUS.GetLeader]'s theory of sound economics. Under the leadership of Comrade [RUS.GetLeader], we will build a prosperous, strong, stable, and harmonious modern communist nation. This will not only bring rich economic benefits to the people, but will also significantly boost the Union's "hard power" such as military strength, laying a solid foundation for the future unification of the Soviet Union and the recovery of lost territories.

name: The Third Industrialization Wave
desc: With our course set, we need to expand the industrialization plan beyond the great cities and allow the smaller cities to reap the rewards of Soviet industry. When we're done, every hamlet in the Far East will become a testament to the success of our laborers!

name: A Coal Mining Boom
desc: While those in the party that sought to undermine proper Marxist applications of economic theory speak of investments by foreign companies in the Soviet Union, we know that our strategic resources are too important to allow the forces of capital gain too strong a hold. That being said, as long as they're just merely under the ground it's hardly of any use to us. We'll expand our excavations of the South Yakutsk basins to bring more coal to fuel our industrial growth.

name: Increased Production Quotas
desc: In order to achieve the goals set by our economists, it's become blatantly clear to us that we need to raise the production quotas in all state-owned factories. While unpopular, steps like this will be needed if we wish to avoid repeating the disastrous mistakes of the last administration.

name: Increased Industrial Trade
desc: With our recent industrial expansions it's clear that we've made ourselves more competitive in the developing markets. By seeking to expand our trade deals with neutral states as well as the few handful of socialist states that still exist, we should be able to give a healthy infusion of cash into our state budget on a regular basis.

name: The Tenth Five-Year Plan
desc: The Ninth Five-Year Plan has been a resounding success. Thanks to the joint efforts of the Party and the people, we have not only defeated domestic opposition and mapped out a model for future economic development, but have also successfully liberated many territories within the Union. The Party has approved the Ninth Five-Year Plan, which will advance the process of transformation and construction in these recently liberated territories. Comrades, forge ahead!

name: The Great Siberian Highway Project
desc: The M53 was a planned highway project meant to link irkutsk with Novosibirsk. Fallen on the wayside due to the outbreak of the Great Patriotic War and with its finished sections tarnished by the neglect of the many petty warlords that occupied the areas of land where stretches of this road still existed, it's truly in a sorry state. Our economists believe that with the right investments, we could turn the old vision into reality and link every major city of Central Siberia to our capital. A massive boon to our economy at times of peace, and an equally great benefit to our logistics should our friends in the west not surrender the rightful Soviet territories they occupy without a fight.

name: Novosibirsk Special Economic Sector
desc: Novosibirsk is an ideal city to establish another SES. Its great industrial and technological capacities combined with its excellent airport makes it a perfect site for commercial and industrial investment. By opening it up to outside investors under a carefully controlled and planned framework, we'll be able to greatly enrich our Union while also reaping the benefits of the technologies that the foreign companies bring to the table when they establish themselves in the SES.

name: Kemerovo's Palaces of Industry
desc: The mighty factories of Kemerovo are a testament to Soviet economic prowess, one that managed to survive several bloody wars and still go from strength to stunning strength. With this great city back under rightful Soviet control, we'll make it the lynchpin for our industrialization efforts in the region.

name: Western Companies in Tomsk
desc: A great opportunity has arisen. Thanks to our improving ties with the OFN nations and the great scientific expertise that resided in the city of Tomsk, there's now talk of western medical companies seeking to establish themselves in the Soviet Union. If we accept, we can expect to be able to advance our own medical research sector as well.

name: Zaibatsu in Krasnoyarsk
desc: Datsun, Toyota and other major Japanese car manufacturers have voiced interest in setting up factories in the industrial city of Krasnoyarsk.If we manage this situation correctly and apply the right kinds of protectionist measures on the national level while reaping the financial benefits on a local one, this could be a great boost to the Soviet automobile industry.
